questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A point on a bow string is in equilibrium. The archer pulls horizontally with 160 N. Two equal string tensions act symmetrically, each at 75° to the horizontal. Calculate the tension in the string.
markPoints: Resolve the two tension forces in the horizontal direction and equate their resultant to 160 N.
Obtain T ≈ 310 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A gamma photon has wavelength 1.25 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. Calculate the energy of one photon.
markPoints: Use E = hc/λ (or an equivalent two-step route using f).
Obtain 1.59 × 10⁻¹¹ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A transparent layer is 89 nm thick and light in the layer has wavelength 356 nm. Light reflects from the upper and lower surfaces; any equal reflection phase changes can be ignored. Explain why destructive interference occurs.
markPoints: The two reflected waves are in antiphase (180° or π rad apart).
The lower reflection travels an extra 2 × 89 nm = 178 nm.
178 nm is half of 356 nm, so the path difference is λ/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Sunlight reflected from a lake surface is horizontally polarised, while light reflected from submerged objects is unpolarised. Explain why Polaroid sunglasses can make the submerged objects easier to see. Include the nature of unpolarised light, what polarisation means, and the relative effect of the sunglasses on the two reflected beams.
markPoints: Unpolarised transverse light has oscillations in more than one plane perpendicular to energy transfer.
Polarisation restricts transverse oscillations to one plane.
With the transmission axis chosen appropriately, the horizontally polarised glare is greatly reduced.
The unpolarised light from submerged objects is only partly reduced, so contrast improves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A free neutron decays. Identify which fundamental interaction is responsible and explain why.
markPoints: Weak nuclear interaction.
The decay involves leptons and/or a change of quark flavour (for example d → u).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A 0.200 g indigestion tablet contains Mg(OH)₂. Add 40.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ HCl in excess. Mg(OH)₂ + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + 2H₂O. The leftover acid needs 29.25 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. Calculate the percentage by mass of Mg(OH)₂.
markPoints: Initial HCl = 0.00800 mol.
NaOH, hence leftover HCl, = 0.002925 mol.
HCl reacting with Mg(OH)₂ = 0.005075 mol.
Mass Mg(OH)₂ ≈ 0.148 g.
Percentage ≈ 74.0%.

questions.subject: Chemistry

markPoints: Record masses accurately / use weighing by difference or quantitative transfer.
Transfer all washings from beaker/stirring rod/container to the volumetric flask.
Use a dropper near the mark and set the bottom of the meniscus on the line.
Stopper and invert several times to mix thoroughly. Any three valid points score.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A Group 2 nitrate M(NO₃)₂ decomposes: 2M(NO₃)₂ → 2MO + 4NO₂ + O₂. A 0.320 g sample gives 225 cm³ of gas at 450 °C and 101000 Pa. Using R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, determine Mr of M(NO₃)₂ and identify M.
questions.modelAnswer: Convert V = 225 × 10⁻⁶ m³ and T = 723 K. pV = nRT gives 3.78 × 10⁻³ mol gas. 2 mol nitrate give 5 mol gas, so nitrate = 1.51 × 10⁻³ mol. Mr ≈ 211.9. Ar(M) ≈ 87.9, so M is Sr.
markPoints: Correct SI unit conversions.
Find total gas moles using pV=nRT.
Use 2:5 nitrate:gas ratio.
Identify strontium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A filament lamp gives a curved current–potential-difference characteristic rather than a straight line. Explain this behaviour using the movement of electrons and the structure and temperature of the metal filament.

The metal lattice ions vibrate more strongly.
Conduction electrons undergo more frequent collisions with the ions.
The lamp's resistance increases, so current is no longer directly proportional to potential difference.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.modelAnswer: Br₂ is simple molecular with weak forces between molecules; Mg has strong metallic bonding and strong attractions persist in its liquid.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: 6(d)
questions.prompt: For f(x)=(x²+1)/2 (x≥0), find the point of intersection of y=f(x) with y=f⁻¹(x).
markPoints: At an intersection on y=x, set x=(x²+1)/2.
Solve (x−1)²=0 to obtain (1,1).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: 7(b)
questions.prompt: For f(x)=sec(2x)−1/x, with x in radians, show that a root lies between x=0.4 and x=0.6.
markPoints: Evaluate the expression at 0.4 and 0.6, obtaining opposite signs.
By continuity in this interval, a root lies between those bounds.
questions.modelAnswer: f(0.4) and f(0.6) have opposite signs.

questions.question: 7(d)(i)
questions.prompt: Starting from x₁=0.4, use xₙ₊₁=0.5 arccos(xₙ) (radians) to find x₂, x₃ and x₄ to four decimal places.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Prove that adding a rational number to an irrational number always produces an irrational result. Use contradiction.
markPoints: Assume rational r plus irrational i gives rational s.
Then i=s−r.
The difference of two rational numbers must be rational.
This contradicts i being irrational.
Conclude r+i is irrational.
questions.modelAnswer: Assume rational result s, subtract rational r to force i rational; contradiction.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: The volume V=(4/3)πr³ of a sphere increases at a constant positive rate k. Derive an expression for dr/dt and deduce its dependence on r.
markPoints: Use dV/dr=4πr².
Apply chain rule dV/dt=(dV/dr)(dr/dt).
Set dV/dt=k.
Hence dr/dt=k/(4πr²), inversely proportional to r².
